'''Claes-Göran Sture Granqvist''' (born 25 December 1946, [[Helsingborg]], [[Sweden]])<ref name=CV />  is a materials physicist<ref name="Miller"/> and  Professor of Solid State Physics at [[Uppsala University]] in [[Sweden]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Kirk-Othmer Encyclopedia of Chemical Technology, Index to Volumes 1 - 26 |date=23 March 2007 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-471-48496-7 |page=xxv |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ziawsTEKsYEC&pg=PR25 |language=en}}</ref> 
Granqvist is considered a pioneer and expert in [[Photochromism|photochromic]] materials<ref name="Bowser">{{cite news |last1=Bowser |first1=Sage |title=Glass Switches from Transparent to Reflective without Drawing on Power [Video] |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/glass-switches-from-transparent-to-reflective-without-drawing-on-power-video/ |access-date=15 July 2022 |work=Scientific American |date=October 16, 2014 |language=en}}</ref> and energy-efficient building materials such as glass,<ref name="Miller">{{cite journal |last1=Miller |first1=Brittney J. |title=How smart windows save energy |journal=Knowable Magazine |date=8 June 2022 |doi=10.1146/knowable-060822-3 |url=https://knowablemagazine.org/article/technology/2022/how-smart-windows-save-energy |doi-access=free |access-date=15 July 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  
paint,<ref name="Everitt">{{cite news |last1=Everitt |first1=Neil |title=Paint-like polymer could cool buildings |url=https://www.coolingpost.com/world-news/paint-like-polymer-could-cool-buildings/ |access-date=15 July 2022 |work=Cooling Post |date=30 September 2018}}</ref> and wood.<ref name="Wogan">{{cite news |last1=Wogan |first1=Tim |title=Super-wood offers way to create air con that doesn't need power |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/super-wood-offers-way-to-create-air-con-that-doesnt-need-power/3010551.article |access-date=15 July 2022 |work=Chemistry World |date=2019-05-29 |language=en}}</ref>

Granqvist is a Fellow of [[SPIE]], the international society for optics and photonics<ref name="SPIE"/> and a Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Science]] and the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]]. He has served as Chairman of the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.<ref name="Cadenhead">{{cite book |last1=Cadenhead |first1=D. A. |last2=Danielli |first2=J. F. |title=Progress in Surface and Membrane Science |date=22 October 2013 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-1-4832-2496-1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qg7gBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA343 |access-date=15 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
Granqvist received the PhD degree in physics at [[Chalmers University of Technology]], [[Gothenburg]], Sweden, in 1974.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Granqvist |first1=Claes G. |title=Superconductivity of ultrathin films (PhD Thesis, Chalmers University) |date=1974 |publisher=Göteborg |url=http://libris.kb.se/bib/570571 |access-date=15 July 2022 |language=sv}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1975, Granqvist was a Postdoctoral associate at [[Cornell University]], USA. In the period of 1976–89, he held various research positions at [[Chalmers University of Technology]]. 
From 1989 to 1993 he was a Full Professor of Experimental Physics at [[University of Gothenburg]].
Since 1993, he is Full Professor of Solid State Physics<ref>{{cite web|url=http://katalog.uu.se/empInfo/?id=AA301|title=Claes-Göran Granqvist – Uppsala University|accessdate=12 August 2011}}</ref> and the Head of the Division of Solid State Physics at the Department of Engineering Sciences, The Ångström Laboratory, [[Uppsala University]]. In the period 1997–2006 he was the Vice Rector/Senior Advisor for External and International Affairs at Uppsala University.<ref name=CV>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ingesnet.org/download/bancorecursos/jornadas/Claes_shortCV.pdf |title= Curriculum Vitae: Claes-Göran S. Granqvist  |access-date=14 July 2022 }}</ref>

Granqvist has been involved in the development of several technology companies, including Radicool and Coat AB (formed 1986). In May 2002, he and others at Uppsala University won the Venture Cup competition for best university spin-off business plan. This enabled Granqvist to found ChromoGenics in 2003<ref name="Andersen"/> with Greger Gregard and other researchers. Granqvist continues to be a member of the board of the company.<ref>{{cite book |title=Annual Report 2016 Chromogenics |chapter=A few questions to Claes-Göran Granqvist and Greger Gregard |date=2016 |publisher=ChromoGenics AB |location=Sweden |page=7 |url=https://chromogenics.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/chromogenics-a-r-eng-web-final.pdf |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref>

==Research== 
Granqvist is a leading figure of Swedish and international science in various fields including [[nanomaterials]]; [[green nanotechnology]]; materials for [[solar energy]] utilization and energy efficiency ([[solar cell]]s, [[Solar panel|solar collector]]s, energy efficient fenestration), [[Electrochromism|electrochromic materials]] ([[smart glass|smart windows]]); [[condensed matter physics]]; [[biomimicry|biomimetics]]; [[photocatalysis|photocatalytic materials]] (air and water cleaning); materials for [[radiative cooling]] and [[superconductivity]]; [[fluctuation-enhanced sensing]].<ref name="Andersen">{{cite book |last1=Andersen |first1=Maj Munch |last2=Sandén |first2=B.A. |last3=Palmberg |first3=C. |title=Green nanotechnology in Nordic Construction: Eco-innovation strategies and Dynamics in Nordic Window Value Chains |date=2010 |url=https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:707181/FULLTEXT01.pdfaj_Report.pdf |publisher= Nordic Innovation Centre |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref><ref name="Hyceltec">{{cite web |title=Hyceltec 2017 |url=http://events.mercatura.pt/HYCELTEC2017/?pag=claes |website=events.mercatura.pt |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref><ref name="Miller"/>

Granqvist introduced the term "[[smart window]]" in the 1980s, brainstorming ideas with scientists from [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] in California to make building materials more energy efficient. Granqvist used the term to describe a responsive window capable of dynamically changing its tint.<ref name="Miller" />
After initially examining thermochromic, photochromic and electrochromic materials, he focused on electrochromic materials.<ref name="Andersen"/>
He has developed electrochromic glass for ‘‘intelligent windows’’ by using coatings of tungsten-doped vanadium dioxide to detect and change with environmental conditions.<ref name="Menéndez-Manjón">{{cite journal |last1=Menéndez-Manjón |first1=Ana |last2=Moldenhauer |first2=Kirsten |last3=Wagener |first3=Philipp |last4=Barcikowski |first4=Stephan |title=Nano-energy research trends: bibliometrical analysis of nanotechnology research in the energy sector |journal=Journal of Nanoparticle Research |date=September 2011 |volume=13 |issue=9 |pages=3911–3922 |doi=10.1007/s11051-011-0344-9 |s2cid=136789258 |url= }}</ref><ref name="Miller"/> 

Granqvist's work as both a researcher and teacher has significantly driven Sweden's development of electrochromic materials.<ref name="Andersen"/>
As of 2021, Granqvist has an [[h-index]] of 70 and has been cited at least 28,400 times for 600 papers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Claes-Göran Granqvist Uppsala University |url=https://www.scinapse.io/authors/2076359181 |website=Scinapse |access-date=27 July 2022}}</ref> 
He had published at  research papers in mostly refereed journals and over 30 books, and has given invited conference presentations at about 250 international conferences and chaired about 30 international meetings.

* 2011, Mentor Award, Society of Vacuum Coaters, "For his contributions to research and education in coating technologies that help enable displays, solar cells, and electrochromic windows."<ref>{{cite web |title=SVC Mentor Award Program |url=https://www.svc.org/AboutSVC/awards/SVC-Mentor-Award-Program.cfm |website=Society of Vacuum Coaters |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref>
* 1998, Award, [[World Renewable Energy Congress]]<ref name=CV />
* 1993, Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]] (Kungliga Ingenjörsvetenskapsakademien).<ref>{{cite web |title=2015 Annual Report |url=https://www.iva.se/globalassets/info-trycksaker/iva/iva-annual-report-2015.pdf |website=Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences (IVA) |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref>
* 1989, Arnberg Prize (Arnbergska priset) of The Swedish Royal Academy of Sciences, Prize for best invention of the year (Sweden)<ref name="Granqvist">{{cite book |last1=Granqvist |first1=Claes G. |title=Spectrally Selective Surfaces for Heating and Cooling Applications |date=1989 |publisher=SPIE Press |isbn=978-0-8194-0228-8 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SJj2rAA4fkIC&pg=PT4 |access-date=27 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Arnberg">{{cite book |title=Who's who in Finance and Industry |date=1998 |publisher=Marquis Who's Who. |isbn=978-0-8379-0332-3 |page=300 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A48cAQAAMAAJ&q=%22granqvist%22+1989,+Arnberg+Prize |access-date=25 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] (Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien).<ref>{{cite web |title=Claes-Göran Granqvist |url=https://www.kva.se/kontakt/claes-goran-granqvist/ |website=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien |access-date=15 July 2022 |language=sv-SE}}</ref>
* Fellow of [[SPIE]], the international society for optics and photonics.<ref name="SPIE">{{cite web |title=Claes-Göran Granqvist |url=https://spie.org/profile/Claes-Goran.Granqvist-6402 |website=SPIE |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref>
* Member of the Regia Societas Scientarium Upsaliensis.<ref name=CV />
* Honorary Membership, Materials Research Society of India.<ref name=CV />
* Honorary Doctorate, [[National University of Engineering|Universidad Nacional Ingenieria, Lima, Peru]].<ref name=CV />
